extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, companies, FFRDCs, and other proposers preparing responses to DARPA Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for preparing and evaluating proposals submitted to DARPA BAAs, emphasizing technical innovation, mission alignment, team capability, risk/cost realism, and DARPA-specific program expectations. Useful for proposers and reviewers to understand what makes a proposal selectable and how awards are decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the proposed technical approach including novelty, feasibility, clarity, and its connection to the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit subfactors: Innovation — Is the approach genuinely novel? Feasibility — Can it actually be done? Clarity — Is it well-defined? Connection to state of the art — how the approach relates to and advances current capabilities. Evaluators look for well-defined, realizable technical plans that advance the technical frontier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission Alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the proposed work supports DARPA's mission to create or prevent technological surprise and aligns with the specific BAA's technical goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal should demonstrate clear alignment with the BAA's stated technical goals and address any explicit metrics called out in the BAA. Emphasis on how the work furthers DARPA's high-level mission (create/prevent technological surprise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of proposer's team expertise, execution capability, relevant track record, and availability of necessary facilities/resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of whether the team is multi-disciplinary (if needed), has prior relevant performance, and possesses facilities/equipment required to execute the work. Demonstrated ability to execute the proposed plan is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: How well technical risks are identified and whether credible mitigation strategies are provided; acceptance of high risk for high reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators expect a realistic risk register that identifies major technical risks and credible mitigations. DARPA accepts high-risk/high-reward approaches, but risks must be acknowledged and addressed with practical mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether proposed costs are realistic, justified, and aligned with the technical approach; overall cost effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a detailed budget justification demonstrating that costs are reasonable and match the scope and methods of the technical approach. Cost effectiveness is considered in selectability/award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Proposal Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Government evaluation practice of reviewing each proposal on its own merit and documenting strengths and weaknesses relative to each criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During initial evaluation proposals are evaluated in their entirety and NOT directly compared to other proposals; reviewers document strengths and weaknesses per evaluation criterion. This supports the Selectability determination and subsequent award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectability Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a 'selectable' proposal used to decide whether a proposal is suitable for award consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A selectable proposal: (1) has been evaluated against the stated evaluation criteria, (2) has overall strengths that outweigh its weaknesses, and (3) has no accumulated weaknesses that would require extensive negotiations or a resubmitted proposal. Evaluators use this standard to screen proposals for awardability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Decision Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered when making award decisions beyond technical evaluation scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to proposers determined to be most advantageous to the Government, consistent with BAA instructions/evaluation criteria, availability of funding, and programmatic balance. Programmatic priorities and funding constraints influence final selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAA Structure and Required Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: What a program BAA defines and the obligation to follow its specified structure, topics, and required proposal sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A BAA defines area of interest, type of award (contract, grant, cooperative agreement), specific topics, required proposal sections, and evaluation criteria. BAAs are open to all proposers who can meet agency needs (industry, academia, FFRDCs, individuals, and certain foreign organizations). Proposers must follow the BAA's stated instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA Program Design Expectations (Heilmeier Catechism, milestones, phase gates)
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA-specific program features and expectations that proposals and programs should reflect (Heilmeier Catechism, PM-driven choices, time-bounded programs, milestones, and independent test/evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA places heavy emphasis on the Heilmeier Catechism (clear justification and measures of success), program manager-driven execution, time-bounded programs (typically 3–5 years), 'go/no-go' milestones, phase-gated funding, potential government-furnished property/data, and Test & Evaluation by independent teams. Proposals should accommodate phase gates, milestone-driven progress, and independent T&E plans when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical Required Proposal Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Common sections that DARPA BAAs expect proposers to include in their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical sections listed: Executive Summary (no jargon), Technical Approach, Statement of Work, Schedule and Milestones, Cost Proposal, Risks and Risk Mitigation, Team Qualifications and Experience, Past Performance. Proposals should present a clear, jargon-free executive summary and include these elements aligned to the BAA instructions.
